wire.headline: Utility firm reports mixed results with planned job cuts and plant closures
sentences: The company saw its revenue increase by 7% year-on-year to reach 4.26bn GBP for the quarter ending 30 September.
Pre-tax profit dropped by 12% to stand at 310m GBP.
The firm announced 850 job cuts, which represents about 6% of its total workforce.
Two gas plants are scheduled to close by March 2027, with one located in Wales and the other in Kent.
CEO Marian Holt stated that the cost pressure has been sharper than expected.
Ofgem has opened an investigation into the company's billing system.
The dividend has been held steady at 12.4p a share.

The company plans to eliminate 850 positions, representing about 6% of its workforce.

ND.headline: Energy Firm Faces 850 Job Cuts and Profit Decline

sentences.text: The company reported a pre-tax profit of 310m GBP, marking a 12% decline.
The organization plans to cut 850 jobs, which represents about 6% of its workforce.
A Kestrel Securities analyst stated that the job cuts will save 90m GBP a year.
Negotiations with unions are scheduled to begin on 4 November.
The union Unite intends to ballot members on industrial action.
The Kent plant employs 410 staff, exposing the local supply chain to risk.
The MP for Deeside has requested an urgent meeting with the company.
Since 2024, 1,200 staff have departed under a voluntary scheme.
The company confirmed there will be no compulsory redundancies before January 2027.
Shares closed at 268p, a drop of 11p.
Kestrel Securities reduced its price target to 240p from 290p.
Ofgem fined the company 1.8m GBP in 2023 over billing issues.
A customer group recorded 3,400 billing complaints in six months.
